lines.text: Do you know the astronauts on the space station drink water that used to be their own sweat and urine?
This is the International Space Station, built from NASA's own 3D model. People have lived on it without a break since November two thousand.
It circles the Earth every ninety minutes. The crew sees sixteen sunrises a day.
Every litre of water has to be launched from Earth. So almost none of it is thrown away.
Urine is boiled at low pressure, and the steam is collected. What's left is a salty brine.
A newer machine dries that brine with warm air, and pulls out the last of the water.
Then everything is filtered, heated in a reactor, and given a little iodine. Sweat from the air goes in too.
In twenty twenty-three, the station reached ninety-eight percent water recovery. Ninety-eight of every hundred litres comes back.
Fifteen countries, five space agencies, one crew. Every job has a name, and someone who owns it.
Orbi Transfer gives your team that too. A task board.
Name a task, assign it with an at sign, attach the files, and move it from in progress, to in review, to done.
